title.narrative: PERFORMANCE-BASED PARTNERSHIP SCHEME FOCUSING ON QUALITY PROGRAMMING, UNDERSTANDING CHANGE AND RESULTS FOR POOR HOUSEHOLDS AND COMMUNITIES

description.narrative:
The SQRIBE programme in the North of Burkina Faso also integrates a climate-specific component, funded by Irish Aid, which promotes climate change adaptation and resilience within education systems, ensuring that schools are safe, resilient, and inclusive in the face of climate risks. The programme is delivered in partnership with local partners where possible, and applies an inclusive approach that considers the specific needs of girls and children with disabilities, working to ensure they are not left behind in education or disaster risk reduction efforts. A climate-specific objective under the SQRIBE programme was designed following the additional climate funding provided by Irish Aid. The project was assessed, and the climate component (a climate-specific objective in each project site) was found to have climate change adaptation as the principal objective, as the explicitly stated motivation for undertaking the objective, and as the fundamental driver. This component of the SQRIBE programme has climate change adaptation as the primary objective. Promoting the objective will therefore be stated in the Results Based Framework to be the principal reason for carrying out this component of the project. In other words, the climate-specific component of the SQRIBE project would not have been funded with the additional Irish Aid Climate Unit funding, but for that principal objective.
However, the project also integrates a significant objective to promote the inclusion of CwD, justifying a mark of 1 for disability inclusion. Teachers are trained with CwD in mind, ensuring their specific learning needs are considered, and school-based activities are designed to be mindful of CwD and take their participation seriously. Infrastructure and preparedness activities are child-friendly and are implemented in a way that is accessible and inclusive, recognising that the resilience of education systems cannot be achieved if CwD are excluded from climate adaptation efforts. While inclusion of CwD is not the principal driver of this component, it is a significant, deliberate objective embedded within the intervention.
